To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gliomas infiltrate into the brain along preferential routes by interacting with the brain ECM and its components, and that these interactions are modulated by a variety of factors that can be targeted in therapeutic strategies.
the extracellular matrix (including its components and its modulators) is a key player in glioma infiltration.
glioma cells use the ECM as a scaffold to infiltrate the brain parenchym; the ECM is modulated by glioma‐associated cells; and the ECM is a key target for glioma treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ECM and its partners in glioma infiltration, with the aim of providing a comprehensive review of this field.
how glioma infiltration is regulated by the ECM and its partners and modulators, and the potential for targeting these mechanisms in order to improve glioma treatment.
the mechanisms that regulate the interaction between glioma cells and their ECM environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECM is a key player in glioma invasion and that its modulation may provide an important target for therapeutic intervention.

the brain ECM and its partners and modulators are essential in glioma cell behavior and that they are promising targets for the development of novel therapeutic strategies to control glioma infiltration.
glioma infiltration is a multifactorial process, and that the extracellular matrix and its partners and modulators, as well as the glioma cell itself, are all important players.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ECM is not just a scaffold for glioma cells, but rather a dynamic and complex network of proteins, polysaccharides and proteases that is actively involved in glioma cell migration, invasion and survival, thus contributing to glioma progression.
glioma infiltration is a complex process, in which ECM and its partners and modulators are key players, and that targeting this process may be a promising therapeutic approach.
the brain extracellular components and partners and modulators thereof play a crucial role during glioma infiltration and that the ECM is a promising target for glioma therapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gliomas are able to exploit and modulate the ECM, using it as a scaffold and a source of bioactive molecules.
glioma cells interact with the ECM in a highly dynamic way, with a large number of players and pathways involved in the glioma invasion process.
a better understanding of glioma‐ECM interactions and the mechanisms of glioma invasion is crucial to developing new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of gliomas.
